input.summary: Official LSE evidence shows the two roles provide relevant policy experience but do not meet the MPP’s stated five-year experience expectation as of August 8, 2026.

sections.title: Finding
sections.body: LSE’s current 2026/27 Master of Public Policy page states that applicants must have at least five years of policy-relevant experience, while noting that exceptions may be granted for outstanding candidates with slightly less experience. This is an admissions entry expectation—not merely a competitive preference. citeturn0search0

sections.title: Applicant experience calculation
sections.body: Using the supplied employment history and excluding the 16 December 2023–3 March 2024 relocation/right-to-work interval: Accra Metropolitan Research Unit, 5 September 2022–15 December 2023: approximately 1 year 3 months; Institute for Fiscal Studies, 4 March 2024–8 August 2026: approximately 2 years 5 months. Combined: approximately 3 years 8 months of policy/research experience as of 8 August 2026.

sections.title: How the roles fit
sections.body: Both roles appear substantively policy-relevant: municipal revenue and social-protection/evaluation work at the Accra unit, followed by research at IFS. They therefore support the required type of experience, but the documented total is about 1 year 4 months below the ordinary five-year threshold. On the official wording, Lena would need to rely on the stated exception for an outstanding candidate with slightly less experience; the source does not guarantee that an exception will be granted. Her First Class Economics degree and quantitative coursework are relevant strengths, but they do not replace the published experience expectation. citeturn0search0

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.body: Verdict: the roles satisfy the policy-relevance dimension, but not the current five-year minimum on their face. This is an eligibility risk requiring an exception assessment, not simply a competitive disadvantage. The application should accurately present the roles and explain their policy impact, while avoiding any claim that the five-year requirement has been met.

follow_ups: If applying, verify directly with LSE SPP whether approximately 3 years 8 months may qualify as the programme’s “slightly less” exception.

sources.title: LSE — Master of Public Policy (2026/27 official programme page)
